mara: Heads-up — deployed the hold-time slew change from #2034 to canary yesterday and saw a weird regression. 95th latency up ~40ms on short requests and KV hit rate dropped ~6%. kernel-selection logs show a lot of handoffs to the older int8 path.

devin: ugh. which params changed exactly? hold_time_ms? any jitter changes?

mara: hold_time_ms went from 6 -> 12, added a small probabilistic spread (slew_prob=0.12) to reduce synchronized flushing. no explicit jitter knob touched.

ryan: can you paste a sample of the kernel decision trace? curious whether sequence-length or token-budget TTL is flipping the selector.

mara: yeah:```
# excerpt from kernel-decide.log
req_id=abc123 seq_len=8 token_budget=64 kv_hit=true selected_kernel=fp16
req_id=abc124 seq_len=8 token_budget=64 kv_hit=false selected_kernel=int8_fallback
req_id=abc125 seq_len=24 token_budget=64 kv_hit=true selected_kernel=fp16
```

mara: note the kv_hit=false lines spiked during the window where hold_time increased. looks like more requests are leaving cache warmup period and missing.

kai: suddenly longer hold_time could be increasing overlap between micro-windows so that stale priming threads evict hot entries? if we delay coalesce we might reduce prefetch density.

lindsay: can we get the profiling flamegraphs for the canary and baseline? want to see whether kernel-switch cost is contributing to the 95th. also add the request-tags for canary so we can filter traces.

mara: uploaded two small snapshots to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/canaries/holdtime-slew/2026-03-16-canary.sym and .../baseline.sym

perf-bot: Canary run 2160000800 -> 2160001400: p50 delta -2ms, p95 delta +38ms, kv_hit rate baseline 0.88 -> canary 0.82. See PR #2034 for config. :warning:

devin: thanks. quick thought: the token_budget target interacts with batching — if more small requests are held longer we form larger batches but that increases the chance of cache churn between prefixes. maybe reduce token_budget for short-seq routes during the canary.

ryan: agree. propose a two-prong canary patch: 1) revert hold_time back to 6ms; 2) add a conditional token_budget override:```
route_filters: ["/v1/generate/short"]
overrides:
  token_budget: 48
  max_batch_tokens: 256
```

kai: i'll run a synthetic load with the canary config and collect kernel-switch counters + KV eviction rate. running now: `./scripts/weight_test --scenario micro-window-surge --rps 1200 --duration 10m --tag hold-slew-2`

mara: nice. also can we instrument a lightweight metric: batch_formation_latency_ms labeled by kernel_variant? want to see if certain kernels cost more to assemble (fp16 vs int8_fallback).

lindsay: added a dashboard tile for that metric under /models/redwood-core. if we get the metric tag from kai's run we can overlay.

kai: short run results: p95 batch_formation_latency_ms (fp16)=9ms, int8_fallback=28ms, kv_evictions/min increased from 12 -> 47. full logs: gs://redwood-perf/quickruns/hold-slew-2/logs.json

mara: that aligns — switching kernels mid-batch is expensive and correlated with the latency tail. suggests our kernel selector is sensitive to ephemeral cache misses.

devin: mitigation options: (A) shorten hold_time for small routes (B) decrease slew_prob to 0.03 during peak (C) add a tiny jitter on batch release to desync eviction hotspots (D) make kernel-selection hysteresis — require two consecutive miss signals before switching kernels.

ryan: D sounds robust. hysteresis could be `kernel_flip_threshold=2` and `flip_ttl_ms=100`. cheap to add and should avoid flip-flop during transient misses.

mara: D + A seems reasonable for an immediate rollout. i'll prepare a canary that sets hold_time=6 for short routes + kernel_flip_threshold=2.

lindsay: add an alert: alert if p95 increases >20ms vs baseline for 3m in canary group. also log any flip events as `kernel.flip` with tags route, req_id.

perf-bot: Created canary job #2160001288 with config: hold_time_ms=6, kernel_flip_threshold=2, route_filter short. Canary live at 2160001500. Results will be auto-collected. :white_check_mark:

mara: thanks — will monitor. if p95 still high we'll try reducing token_budget to 48 and lowering slew_prob.

devin: ping me if you want me to roll the rollback quickly.

ryan: if canary looks good, plan a staged rollout with 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours. include a quick migration step to warm KV for hot prefixes if needed.

mara: noted. i'll post a short postmortem if this becomes a regression. for now tracking in #infra-ops ticket 4421.

kai: uploading collected traces now. will tag with `kernel-hysteresis-test`.

perf-bot: Canary early snapshot (2160001600): p50 -1ms, p95 +7ms, kv_hit 0.86. Continuing collection.

lindsay: nice improvement already. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
